speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Could you describe what happens right before you become unresponsive, and how long these episodes last? Also, do you remember anything during these times?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of head injuries, seizures, or any family history of epilepsy? I also need to know if these episodes happen more frequently at night or during specific activities like reading or playing video games.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: EEG. Do you experience any other symptoms like muscle jerking, loss of bladder control, or tongue biting during these episodes?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electroencephalogram (EEG) Findings: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG confirms focal activity in your temporal lobes, which aligns with the aura and post-episode confusion you described. Given the specific findings of interictal spikes and the clinical presentation of facial grimacing with a muddy taste, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Focal Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
